title: Times Tables to 10
subtitle: Factors 0 to 10
bounds: Factors 0 to 10. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: a fact with 0, 1, 2, 5 or 10 (85 prompts); T2 R: facts from 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 with a 3, 4 or 9 (27; at least 8 with both factors in 3, 4, 9); T3 R: a 6, 7 or 8 (27; at least 8 with both in 6, 7, 8); T4 C: at least 12 from 3, 4, 6-9 on both factors, else any factors 2-10 (81 prompts); T5 S: at least 12 from 3, 4, 6-9 on both factors, plus C from the same (72). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier.

tiers.name: Times 0, 1, 2, 5, 10
tiers.description: Times 0, 1, 2, 5 and 10. Zero, itself, doubles, half of ten, add a zero.

tiers.name: Times 3, 4, 9
tiers.description: Times 3, 4 and 9. Double for 4s, ten minus one for 9s.

tiers.name: Times 6, 7, 8
tiers.description: Times 6, 7 and 8. Split a 6, 7 or 8 into 5 and the rest.

tiers.name: Missing factors
tiers.description: Missing factor: 6 × ? = 42. Ask what times 6 makes 42.

tiers.name: Missing first factors
tiers.description: First factor missing: ? × 6 = 42, or a missing second factor. Facts with 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9.

GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.
